# Independent audit: explicit thin-support and nearly opposite critical caps

Audited in full:

- `candidate 2bb708ddf25004e0`;
- `candidate c55eff377f981f2e`.

Both PASS with no mathematical repair required. Their explicit shape,
contact, global-comparison, and normalization hypotheses remain necessary
for the statements being proved. Neither source claims arbitrary OC.

## 1. Support contact, covers, and genuine criticality

Zero B-volume implies its cutting threshold is at least its support
value. If it were strictly larger, moving that threshold slightly down
keeps the B cap empty in measure, while the opposite A threshold moves
up and strictly reduces a proper A cap. The middle threshold and the
actual source remain fixed. Thus true ambient criticality forces an
actual B support cut; this argument does not require a positive-length
support facet. Properness is used precisely for strict A mass loss.

The resulting endpoint A thresholds are2u_i.y-h_B(u_i). Their weighted
sum under a positive dependence of the continuous normals is negative,
because the support values exceed the values at an interior B point.
Consequently their captures cover the whole continuous space. The middle
traces also cover by positive dependence. All trace normals are nonzero,
so their ordinary d-volume boundary mass is zero.

The ordinary cover profiles are therefore applied to actual covers of
A and K, with the sorted orders reversed correctly. Finite fixed-normal
tilts equalize endpoint volumes; when the common volume is positive,
BM of their ACTUAL captured midpoint gives t<=q, and when it is zero
the inequality is trivial. Genuine depth criticality then gives
U_i<=2q_i and U_i<=2Q/3. No stationary-but-noncritical menu is substituted.

## 2. Planar normalization and compatible radius

A maximum-area inscribed triangle exists by compactness and has positive
area. The absolute determinant of a one-vertex replacement equals the
absolute corresponding barycentric coordinate times its original area.
Thus all barycentric coordinates of B after normalization have absolute
value at most one. The ordinary coordinate square[-1,1]^2 then contains
B and the standard triangle is inside B, giving1/2<=b<=4.
After translation by(1/3,1/3), the triangle's nearest side is at distance
1/(3sqrt2)>1/5, and the shifted square has radius4sqrt2/3<2. This proves
both inclusions in the source. The same affine map is applied to all
continuous fibers, so all volumes and all cap masses scale by one
positive determinant; no integer coordinate changes.

Compatibility with the contained ball gives, for every p in A, a ball
of radius1/10 centered at p/2 in K. Its perpendicular diameter and any
x in K span a triangle of area|x-p/2|/10 inside K. Hence the bound
|x-p/2|<=10k is valid without any false area-to-diameter implication.
It implies both K-y and2y-A are contained in the radiusR=20k ball.
The bad-target cap profiles give Q<=4b/7, and the actual middle-centroid
comparison gives k<=9b/7, so R<=180b/7 exactly.

## 3. Angular estimate and the planar strict contradiction

Minimal positive rank-two dependence puts the three cyclic angular gaps
strictly in(0,pi). If their maximum is pi-tau, then0<tau<=pi/3 and every
gap lies in[2tau,pi-tau]. Therefore each sine is at least sin tau.
The two-normal inverse matrix estimate bounds all support-triangle
vertices by4/sin tau. Its area is at most twice the squared radius,
giving |T|<=32/sin^2 tau. Since b>=1/2,

    sin tau<=8sqrt(b/|T|),
    delta=|u_i+u_j|<=16sqrt(b/|T|).

The threshold b/|T|<=2^-40 therefore gives delta<=2^-16.

If an A point misses both selected caps, c=2y-x satisfies
(u_i+u_j).c>h_i+h_j>=2/5. But |c|<=R and

    delta R<=720/(7 times65536)<2/5.

Thus the two A caps cover A EXACTLY. A middle point missing both has
its u_i-coordinate in(-delta R,0), so the missed part lies in a strip
of width delta R in the radiusR disk and has area at most E=2delta R^2.
The normalized upper estimate is

    E/b<=259200/(49 times65536)=2025/25088<1/9.

Summing the two actual critical masses gives M<=b+2Q+E. The bad target
and the B-centroid comparison give E>=Q/4>=b/9, a contradiction.
All signs are strict in the needed direction. Closed cap boundaries
are null; no positive boundary mass is discarded.

## 4. All-dimensional cone radius and cap-pair criterion

For d>=2, the contained B ball of radiusr gives a radiusr/2 ball in
K centered at p/2 for every p in A. A perpendicular(d-1)-ball inside
it and an arbitrary x in K span a cone with exact volume

    [omega_(d-1)(r/2)^(d-1)/d]|x-p/2|.

Thus |x-p/2|<=L/2, where
L=d2^d k/(omega_(d-1)r^(d-1)). This gives both radiusL inclusions
K-y and2y-A. The factor2^d, including the final factor two from
centering around y, is correct.

If delta L<=2r, missing both A caps would give a strictly larger
inner product than2r, so the A cover is exact even at equality in
this hypothesis. The missed K region is a strip of width delta L
in the radiusL ball. Each perpendicular section has volume at most
omega_(d-1)L^(d-1), giving E=omega_(d-1)delta L^d.
The bad target and Q>=Gamma b imply

    E>=(1/Gamma-2)Q>=(1-2Gamma)b.

Since d>=2 has Gamma<1/2, the source's strict upper bound contradicts
this. Dimension one is correctly excluded from this angular criterion.

## 5. The explicit dimension-only threshold

The maximum-inscribed-simplex normalization is valid in every d for the
same determinant-replacement reason. It gives B containing a ball of
radius r=1/((d+1)sqrt d), and1/d!<=b<=2^d. The nearest standard-simplex
facet is sum x_i=1; its centroid distance is exactly r.

The top-three ordinary profiles use at least three actual caps. Their
indices may overlap at d=2, but discarding negative terms and bounding
all three positive terms by (2+kappa)w=w/Gamma remains valid. Thus

    a+k<=5Q/(3Gamma).

Together with the bad target this implies Q<=3Gamma b, and the middle
comparison gives k<=3b. Therefore L<=C_d b with the stated C_d.
For the stated epsilon_d and normalized unit normals, the two estimates
are exactly

    delta L<=epsilon_d C_d2^d<=r<2r,
    E/b<=omega_(d-1)epsilon_d C_d^d2^(d(d-1))
                                  <=(1-2Gamma)/2<1-2Gamma.

The power2^(d(d-1)) arises from b^(d-1), not b^d, after dividing by b.
The inequalities remain strict where needed even with delta=epsilon_d.
Euclidean angles are tested ONLY after the specified common continuous
affine transformation. No affine invariance of the original angles is
claimed. The note correctly avoids asserting that a large enclosing
simplex in higher dimension forces an almost opposite pair.

## 6. Verification

`supporting computation verify_thin_support_and_antipodal_audit_slab_recovery.py` independently
checks the exact planar constants, the cone-radius coefficient, and the
symbolic threshold substitutions. These finite checks supplement the
classical proofs audited above; they do not replace the all-dimensional
arguments or assert the existence of a general critical normal pair.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
